replace_all: False
old_string:
state = m.get_state()
m2 = LabelLexiconSnapMemory(FakeLLM("[罪名]失火<eoa>"))
m2.set_state(state)
assert len(m2.examples) == len(m.examples)
assert m2.lexicon == m.lexicon
assert sorted(m2.label_counts.items()) == sorted(m.label_counts.items())
ans3, _ = m2.predict("事实:被告人盗窃路灯电缆线，破坏电力设备。")
print("round-trip predict ->", repr(ans3), "| lexicon restored:", len(m2.lexicon))
assert ans3 == ans2, (ans3, ans2)

new_string:
state = m.get_state()
# Restoring into an instance backed by the SAME fake model must reproduce the
# identical prediction -- that isolates state fidelity from model stochasticity.
m2 = LabelLexiconSnapMemory(FakeLLM("[罪名]破坏电力设施<eoa>"))
m2.set_state(state)
assert len(m2.examples) == len(m.examples)
assert m2.lexicon == m.lexicon
assert sorted(m2.label_counts.items()) == sorted(m.label_counts.items())
ans3, meta3 = m2.predict("事实:被告人盗窃路灯电缆线，破坏电力设备。")
print("round-trip predict ->", repr(ans3), "| lexicon restored:", len(m2.lexicon))
assert ans3 == ans2, (ans3, ans2)
assert meta3["num_selected"] == meta2["num_selected"]

# And a cold instance must not be affected by restored state elsewhere.
m3 = LabelLexiconSnapMemory(FakeLLM("[罪名]失火<eoa>"))
ans4, _ = m3.predict("事实:被告人焚烧秸秆引发山火。")
print("unrelated instance predict ->", repr(ans4))
assert ans4 == "失火", ans4
